base_case: Over the next 30-60 days, the base case is range-bound chop to further downside: price has fully retraced the May-June advance, sitting on the 61.8% fib (~7,368) and barely above a flattening 50-day SMA (~7,349), with breadth and credit in Extreme Fear and a 78.6% down-first Monte Carlo edge. The mechanically intact bull skeleton (50d > 200d, +6.4% over the 200-day) argues against a crash, but valuation support now sits above spot, so the path of least resistance is a test of the 7,351 caution/liquidation zone and, if broken, the 7,199 nervous zone.

what_changed_today: Active swing high re-anchored to 7,577.92 (6/15) and swing low to 7,237.85 (6/09); close 7,358.22 sits essentially on the 61.8% fib (7,368) after fully retracing the active leg, with the engine re-anchoring downside to the 7,350.58 caution/liquidation zone.
Price cushion over the 50-day SMA collapsed to just ~0.13% (7,358 vs 7,349) — the 50-day is now flattening and acting as the last line of mechanical support.
ERP edged to ~0.58%, just off the 0.5% valuation ceiling; the 0.5% ERP re-entry floor (7,473) sits well ABOVE spot, so price remains below valuation-confirmed support.
VIX cooled to 18.63 (down from the recent high-zone reading), back inside the 15-20 standard regime near its flat 50-day MA — the volatility backdrop is benign with no capitulation washout.
Monte Carlo edge remains decisively down-first at 78.6% (up from 76.5%), failing all regime thresholds; if 7,351 breaks, P(7,199)=78%.
narrative_summary: SPX closed 7,358.22, having fully retraced the May-June advance to sit right on the 61.8% fib and barely above a flattening 50-day SMA, with a weak bottom-third close. The bull skeleton is still mechanically intact (50d > 200d, +6.4% over the 200-day), but breadth (McClellan 883, Extreme Fear) and credit (junk spread 1.37%, wide) have refused to confirm price for 8+ sessions, ERP is pinned near the 0.5% valuation ceiling with support above spot, and Monte Carlo is a decisive 78.6% down-first. This is a topping-zone tape where defensive patience with a trim bias — not re-entry — is the only justified posture into the next session.

primary_tension: A mechanically intact bull skeleton (50d > 200d, +6.4% over the 200-day, benign VIX) is colliding with a fully-retraced active leg sitting on the 61.8% fib and a flattening 50-day, a weak distribution close, an ERP at the 0.5% valuation ceiling with support above spot, 8+ sessions of Extreme Fear breadth and wide credit refusing to confirm, and a 78.6% down-first Monte Carlo edge — leaving defensive patience with a trim bias, not re-entry, as the only justified posture.
